purpose: Human-only concept exploration; no production models changed

prompts.a-improviser:
Create a polished landscape character design sheet for ZipperCrew, an original stylized real-time 3D game about a crew working together. INPUT ROLES: reference 1 is the ACTUAL current cast; preserve its broad chunky game proportions and simple tactile matte material language, but redesign ONLY the HUMAN. Other references are inspiration only: extract lively hair, adventurous clothing layering, listening body language and impish warmth. Never copy the photographed man's face, exact garments, or hairstyle; never copy the cartoon's face, red star hair, yellow shirt/green shorts, proportions, or barefoot design. Original young ADULT male-presenting HUMAN, no beard/moustache, no celebrity resemblance, no child/chibi, no feminine generic cute avatar. Human should feel organic and expressive alongside these robots. More defined jaw/nose/eyebrows and smaller eyes than a baby mascot, compact game proportions but enough torso/legs to read young adult. Warm intelligent amused expression, listening rather than commanding. Purple/plum is dominant clothing identity. Crisp authored stylized 3D meshes, sculptural hair masses, broad clear color blocks, restrained materials, coherent soft directional key light and grounded shadows. Not painterly, photoreal, fashion drawing, office avatar, or a famous franchise imitation.
DELIVERABLE: one landscape concept sheet on light neutral warm-gray background with FIVE well-separated full-body views of EXACTLY THE SAME character and clothing. Four LARGE poses in a balanced 2x2 arrangement and one small solid BLACK silhouette inset at right/bottom, leaving air around limbs. Include a concise concept title and labels: 'Neutral', 'Orchestrating', 'At laptop', 'Expressive idle', 'Silhouette'. Neutral three-quarter view; expressive open-handed listening/directing orchestration pose without baton; clearly SEATED on a simple stool AT AN OPEN LAPTOP on small minimal desk, hands interacting with keys and feet grounded; characteristic expressive idle with chosen prop; black solid silhouette of standing characteristic pose. All clothing/hair must be consistent between views. No robots on this sheet. Readable production concept rather than poster; no marketing copy. All poses fully inside image.
CONCEPT A · The Improviser:
Asymmetrical mass of warm chestnut-auburn loose sculptural curls, taller over left temple, one lively stray lock sweeping up, one brow arched. Young adult with slightly long warm face, medium warm skin, bright curious sideways glance and asymmetric half smile. Loose plum open overshirt with rolled cuffs over a saffron knitted sleeveless layer and muted turquoise tee; small irregular coral stitching/panel only on one sleeve; navy cropped tapered trousers, generous cream/coral sneakers. Relaxed diagonal silhouette, hips offset, forward listening head tilt; hands broad and expressive, one hovering open in a gentle beat cue. Prop: compact fold-open teal digital folio with abstract crew dots, not musical notes. Idle: tuck folio under elbow and two fingers raised as if a new idea arrived. Creative musician/researcher energy from clothing combinations without copying any reference garment. Youthful ADULT, no tidy coiffure.

CONCEPT C · The Ensemble Listener:
Balanced strongest orchestrator: chunky but young adult proportions, welcoming elongated face with a definite small jaw, warm amber-brown skin, heavy expressive brows and amused half smile, eye line visibly listening to someone just outside sheet. PUSH DISTINCTIVENESS: replace the ordinary short jacket shape with a relaxed THIGH-LENGTH PLUM KNITTED OPEN CARDIGAN, asymmetric draping hem with ochre lining, wide rolled sleeves over a burnt coral shirt; indigo tapered trousers all the way to ankle, no cargo shorts. Hair is a broad asymmetrical tumble of clearly looping corkscrew curls, copper highlights, longer behind one ear, emphatically NOT a standard upward quiff. One cuff teal and one ochre. A slim round ear cuff without huge headphones. Curved, open and listening silhouette. Adult facial bone structure, smaller expressive eyes. This is a cardigan-and-folio concept, not generic purple utility jacket.

CONCEPT D · The Offbeat:
Bold original design: slightly taller young adult, broad upper silhouette from a boxy PLUM sleeveless quilted artist gilet over a cobalt/lavender striped long-sleeve tee, sleeves pushed up revealing apricot cuffs; dark aubergine wide tapered work trousers, asymmetrically laced large cream shoes with teal tongues. Not wizard or circus costume. Large asymmetrical auburn hair rising in three chunky folded-wave CURLS like loose sculpted ribbons, one long loose side curl almost to cheek, darker roots; distinct from spiky cartoon hair. Deep warm brown skin, elongated face, strong nose, expressive crooked eyebrows, mischievous knowing smile with no giant baby eyes. Prop an ochre clamshell mini-laptop/digital score with chunky handle, no phone. Human has relaxed springy stance, one knee soft, torso twisted naturally toward crew. Orchestrating pose one broad open hand sketches a gentle offbeat cue while device is cradled in opposite forearm. Expressive idle balances device on bent knee while listening with head tilted and free hand open. Tasteful eclectic textile blocking, adult creative charm, not overdesigned fantasy gear.
Make the folded-wave hair HUGE and visibly offset sideways, designed as a few large grooved swoops, not many small round curls. Boxy gilet and broad trousers make a bold trapezoidal silhouette, strong and compact enough to stand beside the reference robots. One ochre diagonal woven trim on gilet and teal/lilac sleeve stripes, no tiny patterned clutter. Playful adult male face, expressive hands.
prompts.b-spark-revision:
Revise this ORIGINAL ZipperCrew Human concept sheet (input1) substantially to distinguish its silhouette from a generic neat jacket avatar. Input2 is current cast for material language and proportional relationship only; no robots on output. Preserve the FIVE-view layout and labels, full-body neutral, orchestrating, seated at laptop, expressive idle, small SOLID BLACK silhouette. Title 'B · The Spark'. Same revised character consistent across all poses, clean neutral background, matte stylized 3D game render.

Make this character distinctly young ADULT male, playful impish but not childlike. REPLACE the tidy tufted hairstyle with a broad windswept DARK COPPER SHAG: 7-9 irregular angular curved locks jutting asymmetrically sideways and back, a long loose forelock, two thin upward flyaways. Big sculptural silhouette, NOT radial red spikes, no resemblance to any existing cartoon. Face slightly longer with defined cheek/jaw and strong nose, knowing asymmetric eyebrow, crooked amused half-smile. Warm fair skin lightly freckled. More wiry body, broad hands, slightly springy forward posture.

REPLACE the neat short purple jacket with a loose asymmetric plum ARTIST OVERSHIRT, off-center fastening, one long uneven shirttail, one patch in coral, one mismatched rolled teal sleeve and one lilac sleeve, a slim mustard shirt underneath. These are bold few panels, not busy pattern. Full-length ink-blue narrow trousers and worn chunky cream high-top sneakers with plum/coral panels, no shorts, no baby proportions. Butter-yellow notebook secured with broad elastic, teal pencil; notebook has abstract crew diagrams, not music notes. Expressive idle sitting sideways on stool with ankle across knee, finger at eyebrow and a delighted 'I have an idea' half smile; neutral is never rigid; orchestrating is leaning in with notebook open and free hand conducting a small upbeat gesture.

Avoid celebrity portrait, existing fictional character copy, exact reference costumes, elf ears, fantasy costume. Original warm slightly eccentric HUMAN creative orchestrator. No uniform, badges, phone or oversized headphones. This direction should feel visibly more unruly and idiosyncratic than the original sheet.
prompts.b-cast:
Create a CAST COMPARISON edit for ZipperCrew. Input1 is the actual CURRENT CAST RENDER: Human at LEFT, orange Implementer at CENTER, teal Reviewer at RIGHT. Input2 is selected new Human B · The Spark concept sheet.
REPLACE ONLY THE LEFT HUMAN in input1 with the original male-presenting Human design in input2. Keep orange Implementer and teal Reviewer essentially EXACTLY as input1: same silhouettes, mesh-like shape simplicity, head proportions, facial screens, antenna, cream plates, orange/teal colors, limbs, hands, feet, accessories, tablet, poses. Do not upgrade/redesign/reinterpret the robots. Preserve robot positions and neutral backdrop, floor plane and light direction. Crop excess blank margins to make all three large and easy to compare. All feet share floor and cast shadows in same direction.

New Human: preserve the windswept asymmetrical copper shag, flyaways, adult stylized face with crooked smile, plum long uneven overshirt with mismatched teal and lavender sleeves, mustard tee, dark full-length trousers, cream/plum high-tops, yellow notebook and teal pencil. Adapt DETAIL LEVEL to existing robot game meshes: broader sculpted hair locks and simpler flat materials, no realistic tiny fabric/lace texture. Keep character recognizable from input2. Human approx same overall height as Reviewer, slightly taller than compact Implementer; head and hands robust enough to fit this cast. Pose with open notebook supported in one hand and free hand making a SMALL open cue toward Implementer, head turned warmly toward robots as if listening; not boss pointing down. Young adult, not baby/child.

Finished image should show all THREE full-body characters side by side, HUMAN on LEFT, IMP on CENTER, REVIEWER on RIGHT. No room or desk. Clean comparison contact sheet with small unobtrusive header 'B · The Spark — cast comparison'. No other copy. This is a concept compositing test, not new robot designs. Preserve current robots over everything else.
prompts.b-cast-scale: Targeted scale correction to the attached B · The Spark cast comparison. Keep entire orange Implementer and teal Reviewer EXACTLY unchanged. Keep all character designs, Human clothing, hair, face, notebook, gesture, title, lighting and backdrop. Human at left is too tall relative to robots. Reduce the ENTIRE Human and held notebook uniformly to 80% of current size, keeping both shoes planted on the same floor baseline. Do not turn Human into a child or change proportions, just uniformly rescale as a coherent actor. His highest hair flyaway should reach approximately the top of Reviewer's cream head spike (within a few percent), his eyes should be close to robots' face-screen level. Update his floor/contact shadow consistently. Move him a little closer to orange robot if needed for balanced spacing, preserving gesture space. All three should read as equal cast members at the same physical scale. Do not redraw robots or invent new details.
